Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.block

Class SinglesStackBE

java.lang.Object
net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.block.SinglesStackBE
public class SinglesStackBE extends net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity
One Singles Stack: 64 single items drawn as a rotatable 4 x 4 x 4 grid.

A slot index is a cell, not a place in a bag, and every item must sit on one directly below it or on the seam with the Singles Stack beneath. A vertical run of these is a SinglesColumn, which is what automation addresses; this class owns one block's cells, its shape, its layout rotation, and a rotation for each rendered item.

Capability exposure is loader-specific and lives outside this class; getItems() is what a loader-specific capability view adapts.

  • Method Details

    • column

      @Nullable public SinglesColumn column()
      The column this block belongs to, or null on the client and for a block being removed.

      Resolved once a tick and held, because a machine reading this block's item handler resolves the column once per slot it walks. See StorageStackBE.pile() for the full reasoning.

    • isValidSinglesItem

      public static boolean isValidSinglesItem(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack)
      Whether Singles accepts this item. Bar-valid items are excluded, so widening the ingot tags narrows what Singles takes by the same set.

      public net.minecraft.world.phys.shapes.VoxelShape getCachedShape()
      Returns the occupied-cell shape, rebuilding it only after contents or rotation invalidates the cache. Shape queries occur frequently enough that they must not rebuild it unconditionally.

    • depositAt

      public boolean depositAt(int index, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack fromHand)
      Puts one item from the given stack into the named cell, if that cell is empty and supported. Refuses rather than redirecting the item elsewhere, so a caller walking cells from the bottom fills the supported ones in order.
      Returns:
      whether the item moved; the hand shrinks by one only then

    • extractAt

      Takes the item out of the named cell and settles the visual column above it downward, drawing items across block seams as needed so nothing is left unsupported.
      Returns:
      the extracted item, or empty when the cell held nothing
